sources.fact: 2021 Shell PropertyManager can diagnose Entire body or Failing faces, report minimum curvature radius and display mesh/curvature.
2021 examples list adjacent-face offsets, small faces/edges, and curvature limits as possible causes; recommends Check and surface offsets.
2021 instructions suggest cut-extrude regions away and retry shell to localise a problem.

symptoms: Shell feature reports failure or incomplete operation at a specified thickness.
A shell attempt fails despite a successful temporary surface offset on one or more individual faces.
A previously successful shell fails after changes to parent geometry.
rivals: Thickness exceeds a local minimum curvature radius.
Opposing/adjacent surfaces collide or an offset passes through another face.
Small sliver faces, edges, three-sided vertex or topology causes kernel failure.
Missing/rebuilt parent geometry or outdated selection changes the intended shell problem.

probes.test: On a disposable copy edit the failing Shell feature; use Error Diagnostics > Entire body and Failing faces, then Check body/faces; note callouts, minimum curvature radius and suspect regions.
probes.conditions: 2021 part document, recorded active configuration and target thickness in mm; inspection does not itself alter the body, but editing/saving the feature can; do not commit geometry edits.
probes.basis: DOCUMENTED: Shell Feature Diagnostics; interpretation of why a callout matters is a hypothesis.
probes.member: not applicable: UI-only procedure; no API member asserted

outcomes.observation: Minimum radius smaller than target wall thickness and callout at suspect face
outcomes.limits: Does not prove it is the sole failure or that decreasing thickness yields a globally valid shell.
outcomes.next_step: On the disposable copy retry a smaller thickness and compare diagnostics.

outcomes.observation: Curvature check passes at target thickness, but Shell still fails
outcomes.meaning: Weakens simple local-radius explanation; look at offsets intersecting neighbours or small faces.
outcomes.limits: Does not eliminate local curvature elsewhere or other solver constraints.

outcomes.observation: Inconclusive: diagnostics unavailable, blank, or feature cannot be edited
outcomes.meaning: No reliable result for this probe.
outcomes.limits: Do not infer valid geometry from an absent diagnostic.
outcomes.next_step: Confirm active configuration, feature existence and reproducible failure first.

probes.test: On a disposable copy, use Offset Surface at the same distance on selected suspect face(s), testing normal direction and opposite direction separately; compare success/failure and visible interference.
probes.conditions: Part in same configuration; offset distance equals target shell thickness (record in mm), direction, selected face and effect; create/remove only disposable reference surfaces.
probes.rivals: Intrinsic local offset limitation versus global intersection/trim/topology failure.
probes.basis: DOCUMENTED: Shell Errors recommends offset surfaces; whole-shell implication is ENGINEERING HYPOTHESIS.
probes.member: not applicable: UI-only procedure; no API member asserted

outcomes.observation: Selected face fails surface offset in one direction
outcomes.meaning: Supports that this local offset is problematic.
outcomes.limits: Does not show it is the only cause or that this direction matches the shell interior everywhere.
outcomes.next_step: Inspect curvature and adjacent faces in the reported area.

outcomes.observation: All selected faces return offset surfaces but Shell still fails
outcomes.meaning: Local operations are possible for tested faces; global coupling remains suspect.
outcomes.limits: Individual offsets do not validate mutual intersections, trims, closure or final shell topology.
outcomes.next_step: Examine neighbours and run diagnostic-cut localisation.

outcomes.observation: Inconclusive: offset cannot be tested or input selection is ambiguous
outcomes.limits: This is not a passed offset test.
outcomes.next_step: Record affected face and use built-in Error Diagnostics or inspect geometry manually.

probes.test: On disposable copy, cut away one suspected region with Cut-Extrude, retry Shell with otherwise unchanged parameters; progressively vary the removed region.
probes.conditions: Part copy; identical configuration, shell thickness/removal faces; document cut volume and compare each retained geometry; cutting changes topology and must never touch production.
probes.rivals: Localised topology/interference versus causes remaining elsewhere.
probes.basis: DOCUMENTED: Shell Diagnostic Cut; causal localisation is conditional on controlled geometry changes.
probes.member: not applicable: UI-only procedure; no API member asserted

outcomes.observation: Shell works after removing a specific region
outcomes.meaning: The removed region or its interactions are implicated.
outcomes.limits: Does not identify the unique faulty face; cut changes global topology too.
outcomes.next_step: Narrow removal using smaller cuts and inspect the boundary.

outcomes.observation: Shell still fails after a cut
outcomes.meaning: A cause may remain in the retained model or be introduced by the cut.
outcomes.limits: Cannot prove the removed region was irrelevant.
outcomes.next_step: Try a different partition and compare thickness/curvature.

outcomes.observation: Inconclusive: cut destroys shell intent or yields non-comparable geometry
outcomes.meaning: No valid localisation under these changed conditions.
outcomes.limits: Do not claim the original model is fixed or causality proved.
outcomes.next_step: Return to unmodified copy and use local Check diagnostics.

limitations: No runtime invocation or model fixture was used for these pilot steps.
Successful surface offsets are not a proof of whole-shell success.
A failed Shell creation may leave no persistent failed feature-tree node.
The installed 2021 Help text was read; no 2021 API signatures were asserted for UI diagnostics.
